perspective:
Arthur’s available information:

- He knows he is Arthur Chung, a plumber with a doctorate, and that he works with Teresa Ortega, a medical assistant, on community service projects. He knows they have a professional relationship with mutual respect and shared commitment, though they have sometimes had misunderstandings.
- While working on the community service project, he observed Teresa working hard and appearing overwhelmed. He felt concerned, believed she needed help, and offered assistance. He heard Teresa say she could manage but had a lot to do; after he urged her to take care and said they could work faster together, she accepted his help organizing medical supplies. He began helping.
- He later believed Teresa was hesitant to accept help because she wanted to prove her capability. He felt empathy and wanted to reassure her. He told her he admired her self-reliance and that accepting help did not mean she was incapable. He heard her say she appreciated that but wanted to show she could do it herself. He replied that teamwork is more effective and the goal is doing the job well. He heard her agree and say she sometimes needs reminding. He said they were in it together and he supported her.
- He then believed Teresa was still struggling, felt frustrated that his help was not yielding results, and wanted to support her without making her feel inadequate. He told her things were tough but she was doing a great job. He heard her say it was a busy day and she felt behind. He proposed working together on tasks instead of just helping her. He heard her agree. He said they would tackle it as a team.
- He believed collaboration would ease her burden and improve efficiency; he felt hopeful and intended to commit to it. He told her he was hopeful. He heard her agree it felt less overwhelming. He planned that he would handle inventory while she managed patient records, with regular check-ins. He heard her agree and say she was glad. He said he was too and wanted a productive day.
- He believed their teamwork strengthened their professional relationship; he felt satisfied and intended to maintain collaboration. He told her teamwork paid off and they accomplished more. He heard her agree it was a great experience. He suggested continuing the collaborative approach in future projects. He heard her call it a fantastic idea and say they had proven they were efficient and effective as a team. He said they should keep it up and he looked forward to the next project. He heard her say she looked forward to it too and thanked him as a supportive colleague.

Arthur does not have access to Teresa’s private thoughts, feelings, or unstated reasons beyond what she said or what he observed/inferred.
